text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the RFC meeting — I sketched a small proposal for reconciling two diverging ideas for the weights read path (manifest-first vs index-first) and how warmup should interop with sharded safetensors. sharing here, want quick takes.

aj: dropping in. tl;dr?

maria: tl;dr: prefer a hybrid read path that treats a lightweight shard manifest as authoritative for shard layout but still allows index-first fast-path when a validated index is present on local disk. warmup should be expressed as a staged pipeline (open->map->prefetch->promote) with idempotent checkpoints.

lin: sounds reasonable. can you call out the failure modes? especially around partial downloads and hotstart race conditions.

maria: yes — three main failure modes: (1) manifest missing or mismatched schema -> fallback to model-level index+heuristics; (2) partial shard file present -> we use a .partial suffix and another atomic move on promote; (3) warmup in-flight while routing changes -> versioned warmup tokens, if mismatch abort and re-enqueue.

sam: what about safetensors header parsing cost? we parse headers for shape/dtype/offsets. that can be expensive for large shard counts. any suggestions?

maria: two mitigations: (A) store a compact per-shard metadata blob (index.json) alongside the shard manifest that includes header summaries so we can skip full header parsing for the common path; (B) cache parsed headers in local metadata store with TTL and file-mtime checks.

lin: ok. and how does this interact with mmap/zero-copy and quantized mmaps? we need warmup to optionally materialize quantized tensors into GPU memory if requested by runtime.

aj: propose an explicit warmup intent flag: fast_warmup: {modes: [mmap_lazy, mmap_eager, materialize_gpu]} that the serving runtime can pass to the loader. loader implements mode-specific behavior and exposes progress via metrics.

maria: exactly. loader API change would be: load_shard(shard_ref, intent=..., checkpoint_token="...") -> iterator of stages or immediate handle. but keeping the wire/manifest shape simple is important.

sam: how do we handle sharding variants — contiguous, interleaved, and per-layer split? manifest should describe mapping at tensor-granularity, right?
maria: yes. manifest entries are tensor-granularity: {tensor_name, offset, length, dtype, shard_id}. For interleaved cases we add a "mapping": "interleaved" and small stride metadata. the index-first fast path can keep a simplified mapping for the most common contiguous layouts.

lin: are we introducing a new canonical manifest format or reusing existing safetensors+manifest approach? customers care about compatibility.
maria: reuse safetensors for payload but introduce a tiny manifest JSON v1 that references safetensors shards and contains the tensor-level map + optional header-summaries. manifest v1 is backward-compatible: if absent, loader tries index-first heuristics and logs a warning.

warmup-bot: observed event: warmup_attempt_started model=redwood/xl-ct4 shard_count=32 intent=mmap_eager token=wmk_9b3

aj: metrics we need: warmup_latency_ms per-shard, bytes_mmaped, bytes_materialized_gpu, warmup_retries, and warmup_promote_time. also a counter for manifest_mismatch_falls.

sam: what about rolling upgrade of on-disk manifests? say we change manifest v1->v2 with extra fields. loaders must be forward-tolerant.

maria: plan: version field + conservative parsing. unknown fields are ignored; new required fields must have fallback inference rules. and we should publish a migration checklist for infra (edge caches, S3 replication).

lin: one more: eviction interaction — if warmup promotes a shard to local store and eviction kicks in, we need reference counting on the promote handles so requests in-flight don't crash.

aj: agreed. implement soft pins with TTL and reference increment on active requests. eviction will check pin count and last-active-time. that dovetails with warmup checkpoints.

maria: final ask: can @aj and @lin take a quick pass on the loader API PR I'll open? aim to merge small changes this week so eng-runtime can prototype. I'll paste the proposed schema in the PR.

aj: on it.

lin: I'll review after lunch. quick nit: in the manifest examples please use explicit shard checksums (blake3) so we can detect corruption early.

maria: added to the notes. thanks. :thumbsup: 

warmup-bot: observed event: warmup_attempt_succeeded model=redwood/xl-ct4 shard_id=3 duration_ms=243

sam: nice. nothing blocking from infra side.

maria: thanks all — I'll open the PR and tag you. this thread can be the reference for the follow-up doc.
